# azurerm

Stores Terraform state in an [Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-introduction) container. The `key` setting names the blob that holds the state file.

This backend supports state locking and consistency checking with Azure Blob Storage native capabilities.

## Authentication

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

The `azurerm` backend needs permission to read and write the state file through the storage account's Blob Storage data plane endpoint. The machine running Terraform also needs network access to that endpoint. Storage firewall rules or private endpoints must allow that connection; Azure permissions alone do not provide network access.

Choose one of these authentication methods:

- [Microsoft Entra ID](#microsoft-entra-id) **(Recommended)**
- [SAS Token](#sas-token) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key](#access-key) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key Lookup](#access-key-lookup) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*

### Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup Authentication Types

Terraform supports five types of Microsoft Entra ID authentication, which apply to the Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup methods.

- OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation **(Recommended)**
  - User Assigned Managed Identity with Federated Credentials **(Recommended)**
  - Service Principal / App Registration with Federated Credentials
- User or System Assigned Managed Identity
  - User Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
  - System Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
- Service Principal / App Registration with Client Secret
- Service Principal / App Registration with Client Certificate
- User Account with Azure CLI only (for local development cycle)

You can supply these types as inputs or through a pre-authenticated Azure CLI session. The following sections describe each type in more detail.

### Data Plane URI

In most cases, you can infer the data plane URI from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.  Refer to the [storage account overview documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#standard-endpoints) for more information on the standard endpoints.

If you are using the ['Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#azure-dns-zone-endpoints-preview), the backend must lookup the data plane URI from the management plane. This requires `lookup_blob_endpoint = true` and the `Reader` role on the storage account.

## Microsoft Entra ID

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and a predictable storage account data plane URI.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `use_azuread_auth` - Set to `true` to use Microsoft Entra ID authentication to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Inputs

- `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` - (Optional, Terraform 1.17) Disable fallback to the provider's `ARM_*` variables. Defaults to `false`. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for separate identities and strict-mode configuration.

The following options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. Required for the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account *(Only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`)*

### Microsoft Entra ID with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect (OIDC) lets a workflow request short-lived credentials from Microsoft Entra ID instead of storing a client secret. Start with one identity for both state access and resource management. Use separate identities only when your permissions, tenant, or authentication requirements differ.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration for GitHub

GitHub's token request environment variables are automatically found. Grant the workflow `id-token: write` permission and configure a matching federated identity credential.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

#### Example Configuration for Azure DevOps

Azure Pipelines supplies the job's token request URL. Expose `System.AccessToken` as `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` and supply the service connection ID with `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` or `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`. In non-strict mode, the backend can also use `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, which the `AzureCLI` and `AzurePowerShell` tasks supply.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc                         = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    ado_pipeline_service_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth                 = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    storage_account_name             = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name                   = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                              = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

#### Complete workflow examples with one identity

The following examples use one identity for the `azurerm` backend and the `Azure/azapi` provider. Expand the example for your continuous integration (CI) platform. Each is self-contained and uses environment variables for authentication instead of the inline settings in the short snippets.

<details id="github-actions-with-one-backend-and-provider-identity">
<summary>GitHub Actions with one backend and provider identity</summary>

Use one identity for both state storage and Azure resource management. This example uses standard `ARM_*` variables; it does not require the Terraform 1.17 backend-specific settings.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container and permission to manage the example resource group.
1. Ensure the runner can reach the storage account's blob endpoint.
1. Configure a federated identity credential so the identity trusts this GitHub workflow. Match its actual token subject exactly and use the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create these GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZURE_TENANT_ID` | Identity's tenant ID |
| `AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Subscription for the example resources |
| `AZURE_CLIENT_ID` | Identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform version satisfying `required_version` in `main.tf` |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root, in place of the short backend snippet. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location during `terraform init`. Both backend and provider read authentication settings from the same environment variables.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.2"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. The first Terraform step initializes the backend and installs the provider. The second saves the proposed changes to `tfplan`. GitHub supplies the OIDC token request inputs automatically.

```yaml
name: Plan with one Azure identity

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # One identity for the backend and provider.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit both files and run the workflow manually in GitHub Actions. It produces a plan without creating Azure resources. For an apply job, supply the same identity settings and storage location, and grant `id-token: write`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

</details>

<details id="azure-pipelines-with-one-backend-and-provider-identity">
<summary>Azure Pipelines with one backend and provider identity</summary>

Use one Azure Resource Manager service connection with workload identity federation for both state storage and Azure resource management. This example uses standard `ARM_*` variables; it does not require the Terraform 1.17 backend-specific settings.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container and permission to manage the example resource group.
1. Ensure the agent can reach the storage account's blob endpoint.
1. Configure the service connection with workload identity federation, authorize it for this pipeline, and match the identity's federated credential to the connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create these Azure Pipelines variables. Enter the service connection name; the tasks obtain its ID. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Service connection name |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform version satisfying `required_version` in `main.tf` |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root, in place of the short backend snippet. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location during `terraform init`. Both backend and provider read authentication settings from the same environment variables.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.11.2"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save this as `azure-pipelines.yml`. Both tasks use the same service connection. The first initializes the backend and installs the provider; the second saves the proposed changes to `tfplan`. Each task receives the job's `System.AccessToken` for automatic OIDC token requests.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # One identity for the backend and provider.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Each task supplies its own authentication environment.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"
```

Commit both files, create an Azure Pipeline from the YAML file, and run it manually. It produces a plan without creating Azure resources. For an apply job, use the same connection and storage location and supply its own `System.AccessToken`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

</details>

#### Advanced workflows with separate identities

Use these optional examples when state access needs a different identity or tenant from resource management. They require Terraform 1.17 with backend-specific environment variable support. Each includes its own `main.tf` and workflow or pipeline. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for the choice between non-strict and strict mode.

<details id="github-actions-with-separate-identities-in-non-strict-mode">
<summary>GitHub Actions with separate identities in non-strict mode</summary>

This example uses OIDC for two identities in different tenants: one for state access and one for resource management. Non-strict mode shares the authentication settings, so only the backend client and tenant IDs differ.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential so each identity trusts this GitHub workflow. Match the workflow's actual token subject exactly, including any organization-specific format, and use the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_TENANT_ID` | Provider identity's tenant ID |
| `AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Provider subscription for the example resources |
| `AZAPI_CLIENT_ID` | Provider identity's client ID |
| `STATE_TENANT_ID` | Backend identity's separate tenant ID |
| `STATE_CLIENT_ID` | Backend identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

The backend accesses the state blob directly, so it does not need `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, even for another subscription. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to lookup the storage address, also supply the state subscription and resource group and grant `Reader` on the storage account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location when it runs `terraform init`. The backend and the provider take their authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. The `terraform init` step connects to state storage and installs the provider. The `terraform plan` step saves the proposed changes to a `tfplan` file. Both steps read GitHub's token request inputs automatically, so only the backend client and tenant IDs need separate values.

```yaml
name: Plan with separate Azure identities

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Provider identity and shared authentication flags.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Override only the backend identity; other settings use fallback.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_TENANT_ID }}

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit both files and run the workflow manually in GitHub Actions. The workflow produces a plan and does not create Azure resources. For an apply job, supply the same identity settings and storage location with fresh job credentials. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments, and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

</details>

<a id="github-actions-with-separate-backend-and-provider-identities"></a>

<details id="github-actions-with-separate-identities-in-strict-mode">
<summary>GitHub Actions with separate identities in strict mode</summary>

This example uses OIDC for two identities in different tenants and subscriptions: one for state access and one for resource management. Strict mode stops the backend from reading the provider's generic variables, so the backend needs its own identity and authentication flags.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only if you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to lookup its blob endpoint.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential so each identity trusts this GitHub workflow. Match the workflow's actual token subject exactly, including any organization-specific format, and use the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_TENANT_ID` | Provider identity's tenant ID |
| `AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Provider subscription for the example resources |
| `AZAPI_CLIENT_ID` | Provider identity's client ID |
| `STATE_TENANT_ID` | Backend identity's separate tenant ID |
| `STATE_CLIENT_ID` | Backend identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

`ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD="true"` does not require a backend subscription ID for direct state access, even in strict mode. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint`, also supply `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` and `resource_group_name` for the state account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location when it runs `terraform init`. The backend and the provider take their authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. The `terraform init` step connects to state storage and installs the provider. The `terraform plan` step saves the proposed changes to a `tfplan` file. Both steps enable strict mode and read GitHub's token request inputs automatically.

```yaml
name: Plan with separate Azure identities in strict mode

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"

      # Provider identity for the resource tenant and subscription.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Backend identity for the separate state tenant and subscription.
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit both files and run the workflow manually in GitHub Actions. The workflow produces a plan and does not create Azure resources. For an apply job, enable strict mode again, supply the same identity settings and storage location, and grant `id-token: write`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments, and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

</details>

<details id="azure-pipelines-with-separate-identities-in-non-strict-mode">
<summary>Azure Pipelines with separate identities in non-strict mode</summary>

This example uses two service connections, which let Azure Pipelines authenticate to Azure. Each connection uses workload identity federation instead of a stored secret, and the two connections target different tenants and subscriptions. Non-strict mode shares the authentication flags and the job's token inputs, so only the backend identity and connection IDs differ.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Create two Azure Resource Manager service connections using workload identity federation. Authorize both for this pipeline and match each identity's federated credential to its connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create these Azure Pipelines variables. Enter service connection names; the tasks obtain their IDs. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Provider connection name for the resource tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Backend connection name for the separate state tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

The backend accesses the state blob directly, so it does not need `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, even for another subscription. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to lookup the storage address, also supply the state subscription and resource group and grant `Reader` on the storage account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location when it runs `terraform init`. The backend and the provider take their authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save this as `azure-pipelines.yml`. The first task runs `terraform init` with the state service connection, which connects to state storage and installs the provider. The second task runs `terraform plan` with the provider service connection and restores the three backend identity settings that the first task exported. The shared authentication flags and the job's `System.AccessToken` complete the OIDC exchange.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Initialization needs only the state identity.
        $clientId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $tenantId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $connectionId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $clientId
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $tenantId
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $connectionId

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

        # Pass only non-secret backend identity metadata to the plan task.
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_CLIENT_ID]$clientId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_TENANT_ID]$tenantId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID]$connectionId"
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Provider identity comes from this task's service connection.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Only the backend identity and service connection differ.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: $(STATE_CLIENT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: $(STATE_TENANT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID)
```

Commit both files, create an Azure Pipeline from the YAML file, and run it manually. The pipeline produces a plan and does not create Azure resources. For an apply job, repeat the connection setup and identity settings, with its own `System.AccessToken` and the same storage location. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments, and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

Both service connections refresh their OIDC tokens automatically. Avoid setting unrelated credential variables in a non-strict job, because the backend also reads generic `ARM_*` values.

</details>

<a id="azure-pipelines-with-separate-backend-and-provider-identities"></a>

<details id="azure-pipelines-with-separate-identities-in-strict-mode">
<summary>Azure Pipelines with separate identities in strict mode</summary>

This example uses two service connections, which let Azure Pipelines authenticate to Azure. Each connection uses workload identity federation instead of a stored secret, and the two connections target different tenants and subscriptions. Strict mode stops the backend from reading the provider's generic variables, so the backend needs its own identity, authentication flags, and service connection ID.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only if you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to lookup its blob endpoint.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Create two Azure Resource Manager service connections using workload identity federation. Authorize both for this pipeline and match each identity's federated credential to its connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create these Azure Pipelines variables. Enter service connection names; the tasks obtain their IDs. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Provider connection name for the resource tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Backend connection name for the separate state tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

`ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD="true"` does not require a backend subscription ID for direct state access, even in strict mode. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint`, also supply `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` and `resource_group_name` for the state account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location when it runs `terraform init`. The backend and the provider take their authentication settings from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save this as `azure-pipelines.yml`. The first task runs `terraform init` with the state service connection, which connects to state storage and installs the provider. The second task runs `terraform plan` with the provider service connection while the backend keeps using the state identity. Both tasks run in the same job and working directory, and each one enables strict mode.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Initialize state with the backend service connection.
        $clientId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $tenantId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $connectionId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        $env:ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID = $clientId
        $env:ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID = $tenantId
        $env:ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $connectionId

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

        # Pass only non-secret identity metadata to the next task.
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_CLIENT_ID]$clientId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_TENANT_ID]$tenantId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID]$connectionId"
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # The provider uses this task's connection; state uses the earlier one.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Restore the backend identity, not credentials from the previous task.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: $(STATE_CLIENT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: $(STATE_TENANT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"
```

Commit both files, create an Azure Pipeline from the YAML file, and run it manually. The pipeline produces a plan and does not create Azure resources. For an apply job, repeat the connection setup, identity settings, strict-mode control, and storage location, with its own `System.AccessToken`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config` arguments, and treat saved plans as sensitive data.

Both service connections refresh their OIDC tokens automatically. `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` keeps the backend on the state connection during the second task, because strict mode does not read the provider task's connection ID.

</details>

### Microsoft Entra ID with Compute Attached Managed Identity

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_msi` - Set to `true` to use the managed identity to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.

#### Optional Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are optional for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This is not required for System Assigned Managed Identity. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_msi              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable. Not required for System Assigned Managed Identity.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Azure CLI

You must have a pre-authenticated Azure CLI session using any supported method.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_cli` - Set to `true` to use the Azure CLI session authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_cli              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable. Azure CLI will fallback to use the connected tenant ID if not supplied.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Secret

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_secret` - The client secret of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_secret        = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Certificate

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_path` - The path to the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_password` - The password for the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth            = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key

This method requires you find the Access Key for the storage account and supply it to the backend configuration.

The Access Key is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `access_key` - The Access Key of the storage account is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

There are no role assignments required on the storage account for this method as the Access Key is used to authenticate to the data plane.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    access_key           = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## SAS Token

This method requires you generate a SAS Token for the storage account container or blob and supply it to the backend configuration.

The SAS Token is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `sas_token` - The SAS Token for the storage account container or blob is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Permissions

The SAS Token requires `write` and `list` permissions on the container or blob.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    sas_token            = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key Lookup

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and is a fallback for when Microsoft Entra ID authentication cannot be used on the storage account data plane.

This method queries the management plane to get the storage account Access Key and then uses that Access Key to authenticate to the storage account data plane. It requires elevated permissions on the storage account.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Configuration Options

The optional `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` argument also applies to this method. It defaults to `false` and can be set with `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE`. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for the Terraform 1.17 requirement and precedence rules.

These optional configuration options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. Required for the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account
- `Storage Account Key Operator Service Role` on the storage account

### Access Key Lookup with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation is the recommended method for this scenario.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

<a id="github-actions-with-access-key-lookup"></a>

#### Example Configuration for GitHub

The backend reads GitHub's job-level token request variables in both modes. Refer to [GitHub Actions with separate identities in strict mode](#github-actions-with-separate-identities-in-strict-mode) for separate backend and provider authentication.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

<a id="azure-pipelines-with-access-key-lookup"></a>

#### Example Configuration for Azure DevOps

The backend reads Azure Pipelines job-level token request variables in both modes. You must also supply `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` or one of its environment variable aliases. Strict mode accepts only the backend-specific alias, `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`. Refer to [Azure Pipelines with separate identities in non-strict mode](#azure-pipelines-with-separate-identities-in-non-strict-mode) for the service connection setup.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc                         = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    ado_pipeline_service_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` environment variable.
    tenant_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id                  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name              = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name             = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name                   = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                              = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Compute Attached Managed Identity

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_msi` - Set to `true` to use the managed identity to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.

#### Optional Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are optional for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This is not required for System Assigned Managed Identity. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_msi              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable. Not required for System Assigned Managed Identity.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Azure CLI

You must have a pre-authenticated Azure CLI session using any supported method.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_cli              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable. Azure CLI will fallback to use the connected tenant ID if not supplied.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable. Azure CLI will fallback to use the connected subscription ID if not supplied.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Client Secret

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_secret        = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Access Key Lookup with Client Certificate

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    tenant_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id             = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## terraform_remote_state Data Source

To use the `terraform_remote_state` data source with the `azurerm` backend, you must use the exact same configuration as you would for the `backend` block in your configuration.

For example to use [Direct Microsoft Entra ID authentication with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation for GitHub](#microsoft-entra-id-with-openid-connect--workload-identity-federation) you would use the following configuration:

```hcl
data "terraform_remote_state" "foo" {
  backend = "azurerm"
  config = {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # There is not environment variable support for this input.
  }
}
```

## Select backend environment variables

~> **Version requirement:** Backend-specific `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables and `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` require a Terraform 1.17 build that includes this feature. Terraform 1.16 does not support them.

The backend stores Terraform's record of your resources, called state. The provider creates and updates those resources. The backend and the provider authenticate to Azure separately, so they can use different identities, subscriptions, or tenants (Microsoft Entra directories).

Set `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables when state access needs a different identity or different settings than resource management. For example, you can give the backend identity access to only the storage container that holds state, while the provider identity manages resources across a subscription. The storage account can also belong to a different subscription or tenant from the resources Terraform manages.

`ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID` selects the identity the backend uses for state access, and `ARM_CLIENT_ID` selects the identity the provider uses. [Configuration Variables](#configuration-variables) lists every supported name. A variable only tells Terraform which credentials to use for state access. You still assign each identity its Azure roles.

### Share settings by default

In non-strict mode, you set only the values that differ between the backend and the provider. The backend resolves each setting by taking the first value it finds in the following order:

1. Explicit backend configuration, including `-backend-config` arguments.
1. The setting's `ARM_BACKEND_*` variable.
1. The matching generic `ARM_*` variable, which the provider also reads.
1. Supported CI platform variables, such as the GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines token request inputs.
1. The setting's default value.

Terraform skips empty strings and moves to the next source. A boolean `false` counts as a value rather than an omission, so `ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC="false"` overrides `ARM_USE_OIDC="true"`.

The non-strict examples on this page rely on that fallback. They share the OIDC settings and set only the backend client and tenant IDs. The Azure Pipelines example also sets a separate backend service connection ID.

### Use strict mode to separate authentication settings

Strict mode helps when the backend and the provider use different authentication methods. For example, the provider might authenticate with a client secret while the backend uses OpenID Connect (OIDC). Without strict mode, the backend also reads the provider's `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` and may try that secret instead of OIDC.

Set `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE="true"` to turn off the fallback to generic `ARM_*` variables. In exchange for that separation, strict mode needs more explicit input: supply every setting the backend requires through `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables or explicit backend configuration. The strict examples on this page set `ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC` and `ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD` instead of sharing the provider's flags.

You can also set `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` in the backend block. An explicit `true` or `false` overrides the control environment variable, even when that variable holds an invalid value. The control variable has no short name and no generic alias.

Strict mode still reads four job-level token request inputs: `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` and `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN` on GitHub Actions, and `SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI` and `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` on Azure Pipelines. Neither platform needs manual token copying. Azure Pipelines still needs the backend service connection ID to request a token for the correct identity. An existing Azure CLI login is not a fallback in strict mode unless you enable `use_cli` or `ARM_BACKEND_USE_CLI`.

Managed identity and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) workload identity also require opt-in. Enabling AKS workload identity allows its native `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` inputs.

Strict mode filters environment variables. It does not change the backend's authentication priority or grant Azure permissions. Terraform resolves each argument on its own in both modes: a direct value does not disable a configured file path, and direct client IDs, client secrets, and OIDC tokens must match their file contents when you supply both.

### Supply settings for each job

Terraform saves explicit backend configuration in the `.terraform` directory and in plan files, but it does not save settings or credentials that come from the environment. Supply fresh credentials for each job. When you enable strict mode through its environment variable, set that variable for every `terraform init`, `terraform plan`, and `terraform apply` command. A command that runs without it falls back to non-strict mode.

## Configuration Variables

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

For more information on when each of these configuration settings is required, refer to the previous sections of this page.

The backend supports the following configuration options. When an option lists more than one environment variable, Terraform uses the first non-empty value in the order listed, after any explicit configuration. The backend-specific `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables require Terraform 1.17. Strict mode ignores the generic `ARM_*` variables but still reads the GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines job-level token request inputs. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for authentication requirements and other opt-in behavior.

* `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` - (Optional) Set to `true` to stop the backend from falling back to the generic `ARM_*` environment variables that the provider also uses. Defaults to `false`. Can also be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE`. There is no generic alias for this control. Explicit configuration takes precedence over the environment variable, including when you set it to `false`. Requires Terraform 1.17 with backend-specific environment variable support. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for the authentication and persistence rules.

* `storage_account_name` - (Required) The Name of [the Storage Account](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_account).
